title: introduce-credential-mapper-and-unify-sdks-backoff-hints
author: Priya Menon
release_notes: Introduces a shared credential-mapper and cross-SDK backoff/streaming hint primitives; bumps python -> 2.1.0, typescript -> 1.11.0, go -> v1.6.0. No runtime breaking changes; ergonomic API additions only.
description:
Motivation and summary:

This PR implements a lightweight, language-agnostic credential-mapper abstraction plus a compact set of backoff and streaming hint primitives to harmonize SDK ergonomics across Python, TypeScript and Go. Goal is to reduce duplicated adapter logic in each SDK (token exchange/lease handling) and give app authors a single set of retry/backoff knobs that behave consistently across runtimes.

What changed (high level):
- Introduced a new "credential-mapper" interface (platform-side) and concrete adapters implemented in each SDK.
- Added BackoffPreset and StreamHint small primitives surfaced in all SDKs; presets include: conservative, balanced, aggressive.
- TypeScript: new fluent retry builder (RetryBuilder) and convenience adapters for promise-based streams; bumps TS SDK to 1.11.0.
- Python: added SessionMapper shim and async-stream backpressure hint argument for StreamingClient; bumps Py SDK to 2.1.0.
- Go: added session factory keepalive and EmitStreamHint helper on the stream connector; bumps Go SDK to v1.6.0.
- Tests: cross-sdk integration tests (local harness) to validate token handoff and backoff behavior under transient auth failures.

Why this is unique / not a large refactor:
- The credential-mapper is intentionally thin: it standardizes the token exchange/lease-check handshake sequence while keeping SDK-specific session caching intact.
- Backoff presets are implementation hints; runtime still defers to host policy for absolute timing. That reduces blast radius for behavior changes.

Commits (summary):
- Add credential-mapper proto and shared docs (Priya)
- Implement SessionMapper shim in python SDK
- Add RetryBuilder and StreamHint to TS SDK, update examples
- Add session keepalive and hint emitter to Go SDK
- Add cross-sdk integration test harness + CI job
- Docs: add SDK migration guide and API reference entries

Files changed (selected):
- sdk/common/cred/mapper.md (new doc)
- sdk/common/cred/mapper.proto (IDL for implementation guidance)
- sdk/python/redwood_sdk/session_mapper.py (new shim)
- sdk/python/redwood_sdk/streaming.py (streaming hint param + tests)
- sdk/typescript/src/retry/builder.ts (RetryBuilder fluent API)
- sdk/typescript/src/stream/hints.ts (StreamHint enum + helpers)
- sdk/go/session/factory.go (keepalive + mapper wiring)
- ci/cross-sdk-integration.yml (new CI job validating token handoff)

Notes on tests and CI:
- Added a new cross-sdk integration job (ci/cross-sdk-integration.yml) that spins up a small auth-mock and runs the three SDKs against a scripted transient 401 scenario to assert retry behavior and token refresh ordering. The job runs in the integration stage and was green in this PR run (see ci_checks).

Backward compatibility and migration notes:
- No breaking surface changes for existing APIs: the new APIs are additive. Existing token providers still work unchanged.
- The Python SessionMapper can be dropped-in to replace a small amount of user glue code when they need multi-tenant token exchange. Migration guide added to docs.

Security review:
- The credential-mapper relies on existing secure token exchange paths; we audited the new mapping code for accidental token leakage and added unit tests that ensure no tokens are logged. Security reviewer (Gabriela Ruiz) signed off.

Operational notes:
- The backoff presets are intentionally conservative by default to avoid amplifying retry storms. The conservative preset is used by default in the SDKs; customers can choose a different preset at initialization time.

CI checks summary and flakiness investigation:
- ci/unit (pass)
- ci/integration (pass) - new job added and passed on the third run after fixing a race in the mock auth server
- ci/lint (pass)
- ci/gh-pages (pass) - docs site update

Merge outcome:
- All reviewers approved, security sign-off complete. Merge performed by squash on main.

Related work and follow-ups:
- ENG-5421 (linked linear) tracks adding telemetry for credential-mapper usage in Optimize. Follow-up PR will add opt-in telemetry tags to help SRE understand backoff preset adoption.
- Future PR will expose a lightweight compat shim for older SDK consumers that expect the previous internal token exchange helper names.

Contact: Priya Menon (author) for questions about API shape or migration.

review_thread:
Ethan: Can we avoid adding another proto if the mapper is intentionally small?
Priya: The proto is only used for the cross-team contract doc and is not shipped as a runtime dependency; we keep the runtime adapters language-native.
Liam: TS API looks good but please add a small example showing RetryBuilder chained with StreamHint.
Priya: Added example in sdk/typescript/examples/retry_stream.md.
Gabriela: Security review - ensure no tokens are serialized to logs.
Priya: Added unit tests to assert no tokens in logger output and updated the SDK logger to redact known token-like patterns.
All: Approve after tests are green.
notes_for_maintainers: This PR intentionally leaves previous internal token helpers in place for one release cycle. After the next release we can remove deprecated helpers. Backport not required. If you see flaky integration runs, increase the auth-mock start timeout by 2s.
